cells.tense: Something here has started to catch, and you're staying with it before it has a shape.
cells.ask: Pick the one beginning that's actually moving, and take the next concrete step on it today, before the whole shape is clear.
cells.core:
Whatever's starting in you hasn't found its shape yet, and you're not forcing it. You're also not sitting it out. That's the balance: enough light to take one step, not enough to see the whole way, and you walk anyway.

Most people either kill the spark by demanding it mean something, or refuse to move until it does. You're doing neither. You're letting the thing gather itself while you stay close to it, and that staying is keeping it alive. Plenty of starts die waiting for a direction that only living them would give. The next step doesn't need the whole picture. It just needs to be taken while the thing is still warm.
cells.sheetLine: You're letting it catch before you demand its shape.
cells.verb: getting the first spark to catch

cells.tense: You're running ahead of what's actually here, bracing for how this all turns out.
cells.ask: Name the one outcome you're trying to force clear, then do today's small thing without it being settled first.
cells.core:
You're pushing for the whole shape at once. Before the thing has begun, you're already testing versions, bracing for how it lands, trying to make the end visible so you can relax. It doesn't relax you. The forcing is what's costing you the start.

Being unsure isn't the enemy here — it's the material. You're allowed to have only the next step. Ask yourself what you actually know right now, not what you're trying to see. What's real is smaller than what you're managing for, and it's already enough to move on. The clearer you demand it be before you begin, the longer it stays not-begun. Let it be murky and start anyway.
cells.sheetLine: You're forcing clarity on a thing that needs to begin first.

cells.tense: The start was there and you stepped back from it, and part of you still stands at that door.
cells.ask: Tell one person the vague version of the thing this week — out loud, unfinished, no plan required.
cells.core:
Something wanted to begin and got held back. Not killed, not abandoned — held. The spark is still there and you've kept your distance from it, and saying it out loud now feels like a step you haven't taken.

You don't need an idea. You need contact — with a person, with the thing said where it can change. Until it's spoken it stays hypothetical, and hypothetical things don't grow. You don't need the energy for the whole thing. You need one honest sentence to one person, badly if that's how it comes out. The rest isn't yours to solve today. The next step is just letting it be heard.
cells.sheetLine: You've been keeping it quiet, and quiet isn't where it grows.

cells.tense: You're already moving on this, and talking about it like it happened to you.
cells.ask: Say 'I decided this' about one choice you've been calling what came up, and keep the action.
cells.core:
You're already in the middle of something — moving, adjusting, making calls — and you keep describing it as if the ground did the picking. The starts around you are yours. The way you're navigating the unclear part is a decision you're making, quietly, in the moment it comes up.

Being unsure doesn't make it less yours. It hides it. When there's no map, no one confirms the turns, so it's easy to file your own moves under conditions. But you're the one reading the conditions. The imagination is running; the recognition isn't. You don't need to announce anything. You just need to notice, once, that the path you're on is one you're actively taking.
